label: Mark van Roojen, Moral Cognitivism vs §2.1…: A free-standing assertion of a moral sentence…
locator: §2.1, 'to call a person virtuous is to express an attitude of approval'
interpretation: The emotivists hold that moral terms in grammatically assertive utterances express attitudes: positive predicates 'signal a non-cognitive pro-attitude', negative ones like 'wrong' and 'bad' 'signal negative non-cognitive attitudes'. Read as: a free-standing assertion of a moral sentence expresses some attitude. §4.1 adds that a descriptivist 'can agree' to this for Geach's second premise, so it is shared ground, not peculiar to emotivism. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
